plan.rule: Each part by the rule frozen with it before it read a picture (rubric/tone-v2.md, rubric/pairs-v2.md, rubric/composition-v1.md; commit ff5e6d3), applied mechanically to the bake-off's 296 pictures read by Qwen3-VL-32B at its pinned weights. Implementation fixed before reading (commit 333c2fb): a kappa needs ten crop pairs, and the questions about a person are judged on the pictures the reader says show one and on the crop pairs where it says both do.
plan.comparisons_basis: as v1: the weight the reader puts on each answer, judged by the yardstick fixed for that

questions_dropped.gaze: two crops of one picture agree too little: kappa 0.354 over 18 crop pairs
questions_dropped.pose: commonest answer (posed_static) covers 97% of the 186 pictures showing a person
questions_dropped.vertical_angle: commonest answer (eye_level) covers 96% of the 296 pictures
questions_dropped.modality: two crops of one picture agree too little: kappa 0.371 over 29 crop pairs
questions_dropped.body_level: commonest answer (upright) covers 91% of the 186 pictures showing a person
questions_dropped.rhetoric: commonest answer (none) covers 98% of the 296 pictures

measures_dropped.mass_x: brands do not differ beyond chance (between-brand share -0.017, adjusted p 0.757)

plan.kinds_note: creative_type is not screened by the rule and sets each picture's kind. v2's definitions did what they were written for: no product on a model without a person (v1: 4), and 14 styled still lifes moved from packshot to campaign (all 14 checked by eye are staged scenes). They also moved 58 of v1's 135 campaign pictures to product on a model; of 24 of these checked by eye, about 19 are campaign photographs, 2 are runway pictures and 3 could be either. So under v2 roughly four in ten pictures called product on a model are campaign photographs (an estimate from the 24 checked). Campaign and product on a model both lead in the readings, so this moves pictures between kinds rather than in or out; the like-for-like comparisons and the split by kind rest on it.
plan.measures_note: Reported beside the rule, not deciding: complexity, edge density and open space are close to one measure (rank correlations 0.88 to 0.96) and agree with the reader's open_space and objects at Spearman 0.52 to 0.57; pleasure, arousal and dominance are three weightings of mean brightness and saturation, which the colour and light measures already carry; symmetry and the saliency-based measures (figure_size, mass_x, centre_offset) go with the reader's arrangement, framing and placement hardly at all (Spearman -0.10 to 0.10), so figure_size is the share of the frame the spectral residual marks as salient, highest for one object on a plain ground, not the size of a figure.
